title: Core MI Functions v3.6
content_markdown: MI (management interface) functions which are exported by OpenSIPS core.

mi_commands.name: arg
mi_commands.description: Returns the full list of arguments used when OpenSIPS was started. As in UNIX, the first argument is the name of executable binary.

return_value.description: an array with multiple strings representing the arguments.

examples.description: Example of usage for arg command

mi_commands.name: kill
mi_commands.description: The command will terminate OpenSIPS (and internal shutdown).

return_value.description: none

examples.description: Example of usage for kill command

mi_commands.name: list_blacklists
mi_commands.description: The command lists all the defined (static or learned) blacklists from OpenSIPS.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: filter and print only rules in a specific blacklist

return_value.description: an array with each object describing the list (name, owner, flags); the "Rules" item is an array with each object member describing the rules (blacklists) for each list (IP/mask, protocol, port, matching regexp, flags).

examples.description: Example of usage for list_blacklists command

mi_commands.name: check_blacklists
mi_commands.description: The command returns all the blacklists that match an proto:IP:port+pattern.

parameters.name: proto
parameters.description: protocol of the check rule - if missing, "any" protocol is used. Note that an "any" protocol check can only match an "any" protocol rule.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: the mandatory IP that is used to match the rules

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: the port of the check rule - if missing, 0/any port is used. Note that a 0 port will only match a 0 port rule.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: optional pattern to check against the rules

return_value.description: an array with the names of each blacklist that matched.

examples.code:
# opensips-cli -x mi check\_blacklists 127.0.0.1
# opensips-cli -x mi check\_blacklists udp 127.0.0.1 5060
examples.description: Example of usage for check_blacklists command

mi_commands.name: check_blacklist
mi_commands.description: The command check whether a proto:IP:port+pattern matches any rule of a blacklist.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the name of the blacklist to check against

parameters.name: proto
parameters.description: protocol of the check rule - if missing, "any" protocol is used.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: the mandatory IP that is used to match the rules

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: the port of the check rule - if missing, 0/any port is used.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: optional pattern to check against the rules

return_value.description: an object containing the first rule that matched, or an error if nothing matched.

examples.code:
# opensips-cli -x mi check\_blacklist net\_dynamic 127.0.0.1
# opensips-cli -x mi check\_blacklists net\_dynamic udp 127.0.0.1 5060
examples.description: Example of usage for check_blacklist command

mi_commands.name: add_blacklist_rule
mi_commands.description: Adds a rule to a non-readonly blacklist.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the name of the blacklist to add to

parameters.name: rule
parameters.description: a string containing a blacklist rule, according to dst_blacklist parameter

parameters.name: expire
parameters.description: indicates the number of seconds the rule should expire

return_value.description: success or failed object.

examples.code:
# opensips-cli -x mi add\_blacklist\_rule net\_dynamic '!tcp,127.0.0.1,5060'
# opensips-cli -x mi add\_blacklist\_rule net\_dynamic '!tcp,127.0.0.1,5060' 3600
examples.description: Example of usage for add_blacklist_rule command

mi_commands.name: del_blacklist_rule
mi_commands.description: Removes a rule from a non-readonly blacklist.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the name of the blacklist to remove from

parameters.name: rule
parameters.description: a string containing a blacklist rule, according to dst_blacklist parameter

return_value.description: success or failed object.

examples.description: Example of usage for del_blacklist_rule command

mi_commands.name: list_tcp_conns
mi_commands.description: The command lists all ongoing TCP/TLS connection from OpenSIPS.

return_value.description: an array with one object per connection with the following attributes : ID, type, state, source, destination, lifetime, alias port.

examples.description: Example of usage for list_tcp_conns command

mi_commands.name: log_level
mi_commands.description: Get or set the logging level of one or all OpenSIPS processes. If no argument is passed, it prints a table with current levels. If level is given, it sets it for each process. If pid is also given, it changes only for that process.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: logging level (-3...4)

parameters.name: pid
parameters.description: Unix pid (validated by OpenSIPS)

return_value.description: A table of processes and levels, or the new global log level.

examples.code:
# opensips-cli -x mi log\_level
# opensipsctl fifo log\_level 1
# opensipsctl fifo log\_level 4 10670
examples.description: Examples of usage for log_level command

mi_commands.name: log_level_filter
mi_commands.description: Get or set the level of the extra filtering applied to log messages for a specific logging consumer (stderror, syslog or event).

parameters.name: consumer
parameters.description: logging consumer: stderror, syslog or event

parameters.name: log_level_filter
parameters.description: the log level filter

return_value.description: The current level filter or "OK" string.

examples.code:
# opensips-cli -x mi log\_level\_filter stderror
# opensips-cli -x mi log\_level\_filter stderror 1
examples.description: Examples of usage for log_level_filter command

mi_commands.name: log_mute_state
mi_commands.description: Get or set the mute state (printing enabled/disabled) of a specific logging consumer (stderror, syslog or event).

parameters.name: consumer
parameters.description: logging consumer: stderror, syslog or event

parameters.name: mute_state
parameters.description: the new mute state: 1 - muted or 0 - unmuted (enabled)

return_value.description: The current mute state or "OK" string.

examples.code:
# opensips-cli -x mi log\_mute\_state syslog
# opensips-cli -x mi log\_mute\_state syslog 1
examples.description: Examples of usage for log_mute_state command

mi_commands.name: ps
mi_commands.description: The command will list all all OpenSIPS processes, along with type and description.

return_value.description: multiple objects, each one containing a process ID (internal), PID (OS) and Type.

examples.description: Example of usage for ps command

mi_commands.name: pwd
mi_commands.description: Prints the working directory of OpenSIPS instance.

return_value.description: a single item containing the working directory full path.

examples.description: Example of usage for pwd command

mi_commands.name: reload_routes
mi_commands.description: Triggers the reload of the routing block (the routes) from the script during the runtime.

return_value.description: none

mi_commands.name: sr_get_status
mi_commands.description: The MI equivalent of the sr_check_status() script function - to get the status of an 'status/report' identifier/group.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: mandatory group name

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description: optional identifier

return_value.description: the readiness, the status and details of the identifier/group

examples.code:
# opensips-cli -x mi sr\_get\_status core
# opensips-cli -x mi sr\_get\_status drouting all
examples.description: Examples of usage for sr_get_status command

mi_commands.name: sr_list_status
mi_commands.description: Command to list the status of the identifiers within one or all 'status/report' groups.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: optional 'status/report' group

return_value.description: the readiness, the status and details for all the identifiers within the requested group, or within all defined/registered groups.

examples.description: Example of usage for sr_list_status command

mi_commands.name: sr_list_reports
mi_commands.description: Command to list the full set of reports (logs) collected by 'status/report' identifiers.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: optional 'status/report' group. If missing, all groups listed.

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description: optional identifier. If missing, all identifiers within group listed.

return_value.description: the reports/logs for the requested identifiers, or for all identifiers within the groups.

examples.description: Example of usage for sr_list_reports command

mi_commands.name: sr_list_identifiers
mi_commands.description: Command to list all the existing identifiers in OpenSIPS or only from a certain group.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: optional 'status/report' group. If missing, identifiers from all groups listed.

return_value.description: an array of groups, each group being an array of identifiers.

examples.description: Examples of usage for sr_list_identifiers command

mi_commands.name: uptime
mi_commands.description: Prints various time information about OpenSIPS - when it started to run, for how long it runs.

return_value.description: three items: "Now" - current time; "Up since" - start time ; "Up time" - number of seconds since started.

examples.description: Example of usage for uptime command

mi_commands.name: version
mi_commands.description: Prints the version string of a running OpenSIPS.

return_value.description: one item (named "Server") containing the version string.

examples.description: Example of usage for version command

mi_commands.name: which
mi_commands.description: Prints all available MI commands from the queried OpenSIPS instance.

return_value.description: an array of the names of available MI commands.

examples.description: Example of usage for which command

mi_commands.name: get_statistics
mi_commands.description: Prints the statistics (all, group or one) realtime values.

parameters.name: statistics
parameters.description: an array of values: "all", "group_name:", or "name"

return_value.description: an object containing the names and values of statistic variables.

examples.code:
# opensips-cli -x mi get\_statistics rcv\_requests
# opensipsc-cli -x mi get\_statistics shmem:
examples.description: Examples of usage for get_statistics command

mi_commands.name: list_statistics
mi_commands.description: Prints a list of available statistics in the current configuration of OpenSIPS.

parameters.name: statistics
parameters.description: an array of the same possible values as for get_statistics, excluding "all".

return_value.description: A list of available statistics and their types.

examples.description: Example of usage for list_statistics command

mi_commands.name: reset_statistics
mi_commands.description: Reset (to zero) the value of a statistic variable. Note that not all variables allow reset.

parameters.name: statistics
parameters.description: an array of the names of the variables to be reset.

return_value.description: none

examples.description: Example of usage for reset_statistics command

mi_commands.name: reset_all_statistics
mi_commands.description: Reset (to zero) the value of all statistic variables that can be reset.

return_value.description: none

examples.description: Example of usage for reset_all_statistics command

mi_commands.name: cache_store
mi_commands.description: This command stores in a cache system a string value.

parameters.name: system
parameters.description: cache system to use (e.g., 'local')

parameters.name: attr
parameters.description: the label to be associated with this value

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: the string to be stored

parameters.name: expire
parameters.description: expire time for the stored value

return_value.description: none

examples.code: # opensips-cli -x mi cache\_store local password\_user1 password
examples.description: Example of usage for cache_store command

mi_commands.name: cache_fetch
mi_commands.description: This command queries for a stored value.

parameters.name: system
parameters.description: cache system to use

parameters.name: attr
parameters.description: the label associated with the value

return_value.description: object containing the value if a record is found or 'Value not found' string otherwise.

examples.description: Example of usage for cache_fetch command

mi_commands.name: cache_remove
mi_commands.description: This command removes a record from the cache system.

parameters.name: system
parameters.description: cache system to use

parameters.name: attr
parameters.description: the label associated with the stored value

return_value.description: None.

examples.description: Example of usage for cache_remove command

mi_commands.name: event_subscribe
mi_commands.description: Subscribes an external application to a certain event.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: event name

parameters.name: socket
parameters.description: external application socket

parameters.name: expire
parameters.description: expire time, in seconds - if absent, defaults to 3600 s

return_value.description: None.

examples.description: Example of usage for event_subscribe command

mi_commands.name: events_list
mi_commands.description: Lists all the events published through the Event Interface.

return_value.description: None.

examples.description: Example of usage for events_list command

mi_commands.name: raise_event
mi_commands.description: Raises an event through the Event Interface using an MI command.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: event name

parameters.name: params
parameters.description: array of elements, or a string consisting of a JSON object containing key-value pairs

return_value.description: None.

examples.code:
# opensips-cli -x mi raise\_event E\_PIKE\_BLOCKED 127.0.0.1 # array mode
# opensips-cli -x -- mi -j raise\_event event=E\_PIKE\_BLOCKED params='{"ip":"127.0.0.1"}' # json mode
examples.description: Examples of usage for raise_event command

mi_commands.name: subscribers_list
mi_commands.description: Lists information about the subscribers

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: event name

parameters.name: socket
parameters.description: external application socket

return_value.description: Information about events and their subscribers based on parameters provided.

examples.code:
# opensips-cli -x mi subscribers\_list
# opensips-cli -x mi subscribers\_list E\_RTPPROXY\_STATUS
# opensips-cli -x mi subscribers\_list E\_RTPPROXY\_STATUS unix:/tmp/event.sock
examples.description: Examples of usage for subscribers_list command

mi_commands.name: mem_pkg_dump
mi_commands.description: Triggers a pkg memory dump for a given process. The memory dump will written to OpenSIPS's log using the 'memdump' logging level.

parameters.name: pid
parameters.description: the PID of the process to perform the pkg dump

parameters.name: log_level
parameters.description: a log level to be used for this dump

return_value.description: None.

examples.description: Example of usage for mem_pkg_dump command

mi_commands.name: mem_shm_dump
mi_commands.description: Triggers a shm memory dump. The memory dump will written to OpenSIPS's log using the 'memdump' logging level.

parameters.name: log_level
parameters.description: a log level to be used for this dump

return_value.description: None.

examples.description: Example of usage for mem_shm_dump command

mi_commands.name: shm_check
mi_commands.description: Only available with QM_MALLOC + DBG_MALLOC. Fully scans the shared memory pool in order to locate any inconsistencies.

return_value.description: current number of fragments.

examples.description: Example of usage for shm_check command

mi_commands.name: xlog_level
mi_commands.description: Get or set the global xlogging level in OpenSIPS processes.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: logging level

return_value.description: the current xlog_level if no argument is passed.

examples.description: Example of usage for xlog_level command
